Seed token = BPE id for 'Hello' (single-token).

Primary oracle: llama.cpp libllama (ROCm 6.3.4) via POST /completion {prompt:[9419], n_predict:8, temperature:0, cache_prompt:false, return_tokens:true}. Decoded: ', I am a student in the ' = [11, 353, 1044, 264, 5286, 303, 279, 220].

V2.2.c.1 first-cut cert — 3-token match bit-exact (11, 353, 1044), divergence at step 3: we produce 4313, llama.cpp produces 264. Pattern consistent with V1.7.4.a on Qwen3.6-35B: argmax-stable for a few steps then F16 drift cascades. Earliest suspects, ordered by likelihood:
  (a) Q4_1 MMVQ accumulation order differences vs llama.cpp's pre-shuffled kernel. Our on-disk ggml Q4_1 pairing is correct (0.00016 rel err on synthetic sweep, 15/15 shapes), but real Qwen weights may have distributions that surface F32-accum-order drift at M>1 batch shapes used across multi-token decode.
  (b) Full-attn layers on qwen35 use Q4_1 attn_q/attn_k/attn_v/attn_output — first time the Q4_1 kernel is exercised on the attention path (vs Qwen3.6's Q4_K). Any shape-specific issue only shows up here.
  (c) Genuine F16 noise floor for 9B dense-hybrid — needs llama-eval-callback per-layer bisect to rule out.

Expect_pass=false is diagnostic — flip to true once the divergence is closed. Until then, ships as a first-token parity gate (3-token match is non-trivial evidence the kernel stack is structurally correct).
